    //==
    // # Bvh3D — raycasting
    //
    // A hierarchy stores no geometry, only bounds and a permutation, so what it
    // can answer about a ray is BROAD PHASE: the distance at which the ray first
    // enters a leaf box. The reported hit therefore carries a real Hit flag,
    // Distance and Position, and leaves the surface attributes at their empty
    // values — IFace is -1, the normal points back along the ray, and the two
    // parametric coordinates are zero. A caller wanting a surface hit tests the
    // primitives of `CandidatesInBounds` itself; that is the second phase the
    // whole broad-phase/narrow-phase split exists for.

    // The parameter value standing for "no intersection". A finite literal rather
    // than `Number.MaxValue`: the limit constant does not survive `--scalar=float`
    // erasure inside a conditional, where one branch stays `Number` and the other
    // is already `float` and the C# writer cannot type the result (CS0172).
    // Nothing here needs the true maximum — only a value no scene extent reaches.
    MissDistance(): Number
        => 1.0e30;

    // The reach of a ray query: MaxDistance of zero or less means unbounded.
    RayReach(query: RayQuery3D): Number
        => query.MaxDistance <= 0.0 ? MissDistance() : query.MaxDistance;

    // The parameter at which the ray enters the box, by the slab method, or
    // the miss value when it misses or enters beyond `reach`. A ray parallel to
    // a slab yields infinities that the min/max pair absorbs; a ray exactly IN
    // the plane of a slab yields NaN, and the comparison then reports a miss.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slab_method
    RayBoxEntry(ray: Ray3D, box: Bounds3D, reach: Number): Number {
        var o = ray.Origin;
        var d = ray.Direction.Vector;
        var ax = (box.Min.X - o.X) / d.X;
        var bx = (box.Max.X - o.X) / d.X;
        var ay = (box.Min.Y - o.Y) / d.Y;
        var by = (box.Max.Y - o.Y) / d.Y;
        var az = (box.Min.Z - o.Z) / d.Z;
        var bz = (box.Max.Z - o.Z) / d.Z;
        var enter = ax.Min(bx).Max(ay.Min(by)).Max(az.Min(bz)).Max(0.0);
        var exit = ax.Max(bx).Min(ay.Max(by)).Min(az.Max(bz));
        return enter <= exit && enter <= reach ? enter : MissDistance();
    }

    // The nearest leaf-box entry parameter under `node`, or the miss value when
    // the ray reaches no leaf. An internal node whose own box the ray misses is
    // not descended into — the pruning the hierarchy exists for.
    NearestLeafEntry(self: Bvh3D, query: RayQuery3D, node: SpatialNodeIndex): Number
        => node.Value < 0
            ? MissDistance()
            : self.NearestLeafEntryOf(query, self.Nodes[node.Value]);

    // The nearest leaf-box entry under one node, once it is known to exist.
    NearestLeafEntryOf(self: Bvh3D, query: RayQuery3D, n: BvhNode3D): Number
        => RayBoxEntry(query.Ray, n.Bounds, RayReach(query)) >= MissDistance()
            ? MissDistance()
            : (n.LeftChild.Value < 0 && n.RightChild.Value < 0
                ? RayBoxEntry(query.Ray, n.Bounds, RayReach(query))
                : self.NearestLeafEntry(query, n.LeftChild)
                      .Min(self.NearestLeafEntry(query, n.RightChild)));

    // The broad-phase ray answer: whether the ray reaches any leaf box within the
    // query's reach, and where. ISurface attributes are left empty (see above).
    Raycast(self: Bvh3D, query: RayQuery3D): RayHit3D {
        var distance = self.Nodes.Count == 0
            ? MissDistance()
            : self.NearestLeafEntry(query, SpatialNodeIndex(0));
        var hit = distance < MissDistance();
        return (hit,
                hit ? distance : 0.0,
                hit ? query.Ray.PointAt(distance) : query.Ray.Origin,
                Direction3D(-query.Ray.Direction.Vector),
                FaceIndex(-1),
                BarycentricCoordinate(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
                UvCoordinate(0.0, 0.0));
    }

    //==
    // # Quadtree2D
    //
    // Four consecutive children from FirstChild, or -1 for a leaf. A region tree
    // stores items at the node that contains them, so an internal node can carry
    // items of its own and its range is always emitted, not only at leaves.

    // The permutation holds every item exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: Quadtree2D): Integer
        => self.ItemIndices.Count;

    // The items of node `node` and of its four subtrees, restricted to nodes
    // whose bounds meet the query.
    QuadtreeCandidates(self: Quadtree2D, bounds: Bounds2D, node: SpatialNodeIndex): Array<ItemIndex>
        => node.Value < 0
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.QuadtreeNodeCandidates(bounds, self.Nodes[node.Value]);

    // The items of one node and its subtrees, once the node is known to exist.
    QuadtreeNodeCandidates(self: Quadtree2D, bounds: Bounds2D, n: QuadtreeNode): Array<ItemIndex>
        => !n.Bounds.Overlaps(bounds)
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.ItemIndices.Slice(n.Items.Start, n.Items.End).Concatenate(
                n.FirstChild.Value < 0
                    ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
                    : 4.Range.FlatMap(c => self.QuadtreeCandidates(bounds, SpatialNodeIndex(n.FirstChild.Value + c))));

    // Every item held by a node whose bounds meet the query bounds.
    CandidatesInBounds(self: Quadtree2D, bounds: Bounds2D): Array<ItemIndex>
        => self.Nodes.Count == 0
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.QuadtreeCandidates(bounds, SpatialNodeIndex(0));

    //==
    // # Octree3D and LooseOctree3D
    //
    // Eight consecutive children, otherwise identical to the quadtree. A loose
    // octree differs only in how its bounds were SIZED when it was built — the
    // stored node bounds are already the enlarged ones — so its query is the
    // inner octree's query unchanged.

    // The permutation holds every item exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: Octree3D): Integer
        => self.ItemIndices.Count;

    // The items of node `node` and of its eight subtrees, restricted to nodes
    // whose bounds meet the query.
    OctreeCandidates(self: Octree3D, bounds: Bounds3D, node: SpatialNodeIndex): Array<ItemIndex>
        => node.Value < 0
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.OctreeNodeCandidates(bounds, self.Nodes[node.Value]);

    // The items of one node and its subtrees, once the node is known to exist.
    OctreeNodeCandidates(self: Octree3D, bounds: Bounds3D, n: OctreeNode): Array<ItemIndex>
        => !n.Bounds.Overlaps(bounds)
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.ItemIndices.Slice(n.Items.Start, n.Items.End).Concatenate(
                n.FirstChild.Value < 0
                    ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
                    : 8.Range.FlatMap(c => self.OctreeCandidates(bounds, SpatialNodeIndex(n.FirstChild.Value + c))));

    // Every item held by a node whose bounds meet the query bounds.
    CandidatesInBounds(self: Octree3D, bounds: Bounds3D): Array<ItemIndex>
        => self.Nodes.Count == 0
            ? self.ItemIndices.Take(0)
            : self.OctreeCandidates(bounds, SpatialNodeIndex(0));

    // The wrapped octree's item count.
    ItemCount(self: LooseOctree3D): Integer
        => self.Octree.ItemCount;

    // The wrapped octree's query: the looseness is already baked into the stored
    // node bounds.
    CandidatesInBounds(self: LooseOctree3D, bounds: Bounds3D): Array<ItemIndex>
        => self.Octree.CandidatesInBounds(bounds);
